new_statements.quote: The following comments on stress placement must be regarded as provisional and are descriptive rather than explanatory. Stress is not phonemic in Tobilung. It is realized primarily by a slight lengthening of the relevant syllable and secondarily a change in pitch and volume. [...] In CVCVC words, many words have final stress, but there are a significant number with penultimate stress. There is no obvious phonological reason for this variation. [...] Three syllable words exhibit less variation. In many words the main stress is on the last syllable with secondary stress on the first syllable. [...] Words with additional syllables also usually have primary stress on the final syllable, but secondary stress may be on the first or second syllable.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and (provisionally) falls by default on the final syllable: words of three or more syllables usually have final primary stress; disyllables mostly final (e.g. [sa'rup] 'wind', [li.'os] 'louse egg') but with an unexplained minority of penult-stressed CVCVC words (['ta.suʔ] 'dog'); CVVC words with identical (geminate) vowels stress the first vowel (['pu.un] 'tree'), and CVCCVC words have roughly level stress on both syllables. Cues: mainly slight lengthening, secondarily pitch and loudness.
new_statements.secondary_stress: In trisyllables secondary stress on the first syllable ([ˌtom.bo'log] 'bird', [ˌbu.lun.'tuŋ] 'rainbow'); in longer words secondary stress on the first or second syllable ([ˌmo.ŋo.ɗu.'laʔ] 'to stick out the tongue', [so.ˌso.do.'pon] 'afternoon', [ˌbam.ba.ja.'ŋan] 'butterfly').
new_statements.exceptions: CVVC with identical vowels -> penult (['ɗe.eŋ] 'betel leaf', ['pu.un] 'tree', ['ɓi.ik] 'young rat'); CVCCVC -> equal stress on both syllables (['tan.'tob] 'fence', ['gon.'tod] 'heel'); a significant number of CVCVC words with penult stress for no obvious phonological reason (['ta.suʔ] 'dog' vs [sa'rup] 'wind', [ta.'naj] 'termite', [ra.'ɗuʔ] 'plough', [ʔo.'pod] 'ten'); when counting, emphasis is often on the penult, especially on the final item of a series (fn. 13); intensification (expressive lengthening) can shift stress position (9.2).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level; author states words were examined in isolation and in various frames, and that 'Sentence stress tends to flatten the word stress.' Whole account explicitly labelled provisional and descriptive. Variety: Toburon and neighbouring villages, Kota Belud district (data 2000-2001).
new_statements.identity_note: Buck 2009 describes Tobilung as spoken in the village of Toburon and neighbouring villages, Kota Belud district, Sabah (data collected Nov 2000 - Feb 2001); she notes a possible dialect distinction between the Kota Belud and Kota Marudu branches (her fn. 2). This is the language-level glottocode tobi1239 / ISO tgb (reference name changed from Tebilung to Tobilung in 2008 per ISO CR 2007-259). English Wikipedia folds Tobilung into a 'Momogun language' page with Kimaragang and Rungus; the statement quoted here is Tobilung-specific.

sources.locator: Section 9 'Suprasegmentals', 9.1 'Stress' (9.1.1 Bisyllabic words, 9.1.2 Words with more than two syllables), p. 14, with footnote 13
sources.note: Section 9.1 (p. 14): stress not phonemic, realized mainly by slight lengthening; author calls placement 'provisional'. Bisyllables: CVVC with identical vowels -> penult; CVVC with different vowels -> mostly final; CVCCVC -> roughly equal; CVCVC -> many final but a significant number penult with no obvious conditioning. 3+ syllables: primary stress usually final, secondary on first (or second) syllable. Sentence stress flattens word stress; counting favours penult (fn. 13).
